title: KV cache slot reclamation and relocation plan to reduce GPU fragmentation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Production workloads with long-prefix reuse (chat and assistant flows) and multi-tenant Dedicated pools are causing persistent GPU memory fragmentation in the KV cache. This fragmentation increases observed working set overhead, prevents effective packing of model activations + KV, and raises unit-cost. Current freelist strategies lead to many small 'holes' that are unsuitable for incoming allocations, forcing extra evictions or larger quantization fallbacks.

This ticket proposes a pragmatic, measurable approach that combines:
- finer-grained telemetry and a fragmentation health metric to detect pathological patterns;
- a two-tier slot reclamation + relocation subsystem that opportunistically compacts in low-util windows using GPU-side copies;
- fingerprint-aware allocation to bias reuse toward matching sized suffix allocations; and
- a safe rollout plan with canaries, rollback thresholds and experiment harnessing.

Goal: reduce effective fragmentation (bytes of free but unusable memory) by >= 60% in representative Dedicated workloads while keeping p50/95 token latencies within existing SLOs (+<4ms median impact during compaction windows).
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation health metric defined and emitted: free_run_ratio, avg_free_run_len, alloc_churn_rate
Background compaction runs reduce effective fragmented bytes by >=60% on lab traces (MPT-7B, Llama2-13B traces)
No regression on p95 token latency more than 10% during steady-state; tail spikes during compaction limited and observable
Feature gated and off by default with runtime config; gradual rollout to Dedicated pools with canary flags
Design doc and benchmark PR merged, and e2e test harness committed
design_decisions: Two-tier free lists: micro-slots (≤4KB) and macro-slots (>4KB) to reduce bin fragmentation
Fingerprint-aware allocation: keep small fingerprint map (128K entries) keyed by (model, sequence_bucket) to bias allocation to recently freed contiguous runs
Non-blocking relocation: use cudaMemcpyAsync on dedicated compaction streams and double-buffer KV pages to avoid blocking inference streams
Soft-eviction thresholds: prefer relocating long-lived small fragments instead of evicting active prefixes; eviction still used when compaction budget exceeded
Background compaction windows configured by GPU-util heuristics (start when GPU utilization < 35% for N consecutive 100ms samples)
experiments: Microbench: trace-replay with 3 production traces (chat, completion bursty, multi-user long-prefix). Measured fragmentation metrics before/after relocation pass.
A/B: Canary Dedicated pool with compaction enabled vs control for 24h under load; measure cost per token and tail latency
Stress: forced fragmentation by allocating many odd-sized prefixes, then run relocation to validate correctness and memory accounting
Comparison: implement soft-relocation vs immediate in-place compaction to measure throughput impact
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — Labs: implement in runtime branch with config flags; run synthetic and replay traces (2 weeks)
Phase 1 — Canary: enable on single Dedicated pool behind canary flag; 24h observation; automatic rollback if fragmentation metric worsens or p95 latency > 10%
Phase 2 — Gradual ramp: enable 10% -> 50% -> 100% of Dedicated pools over 2 weeks with monitoring dashboards
Phase 3 — GA: enable by default for Dedicated and opt-in for Hosted; update docs and add console controls
tradeoffs_and_risks: Relocation copies consume GPU memory bandwidth and may slightly increase p50 latency during compaction windows — mitigated by scheduling on low-util windows and using async streams
Additional metadata (fingerprint map / freelist tiers) costs a small CPU/GPU-resident table; risk of added complexity in allocator codepath
Aggressive compaction could interfere with real-time SLOs; default is conservative and gated behind heuristics
Cross-shard relocation must preserve model semantics (KV ordering) — relocation will avoid moving live entries currently referenced by active execution contexts
implementation_notes: Allocator changes will live behind AllocConfig.compaction_enabled flag
Introduce new telemetry at token-granularity emission points to reduce sampling noise
Use pooled cuda streams for compaction; ensure stream priorities lower than inference streams
Unit tests: deterministic relocation correctness; fuzz tests for concurrency with ongoing allocations
